questions: Did the slalom finish any trials, or did its line_loss_events fall to 1.0 or below with progress above 0.26?
Did the s-bend hold 19 or more finishes, with line losses at or below 0.55?
Did the oval still finish 20 of 20, and did its max_error stay near 0.017? If it rose, the extra look-ahead is adding lag, so y 0.07 should be restored.
If the slalom is still at its max_error floor, is the remaining limit controller gain, so the next step should be a controller change rather than geometry?

intent: Restore the best measured inertia setting (mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.10 m, from iteration 6) and test whether a further look-ahead step (sensor y 0.07 to 0.075) can lift the slalom off its max_error floor without costing the s-bend or oval. Only sensor y changes from iteration 6.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that mass 0.5 kg reversed the s-bend gain (19 to 18 finishes, losses 0.55 to 0.85), so inertia is at its useful limit near 0.6 kg with body_length 0.10 m. The slalom has been unchanged across all inertia changes, so the next geometry test is look-ahead alone. If that does not move the slalom, geometry is near its limit and the remaining work is in the controller.
rationale: Iteration 7 tested mass 0.5 kg at body_length 0.10 m, and it was worse than iteration 6. The s-bend fell from 19 to 18 finishes, line losses rose from 0.55 to 0.85, and progress fell from 0.996 to 0.965. Oscillation stayed low at 0.31, so the jitter rule was not triggered, but the inertia benefit has reversed. The score dropped from 658 to 642. The best measured geometry is therefore iteration 6, so I restore mass to 0.6 kg and keep body_length 0.10 m. The oval stayed at 20 of 20 with max_error 0.017 and oscillation 0.22, and the slalom is unchanged at 0 of 20 finishes with max_error at the 0.063 floor. The slalom has not responded to any inertia change, so the remaining untested geometry lever on its alternating bends is sensor look-ahead. Iteration 2 (y 0.07, track 0.10) gave the best slalom line-loss count (1.0), and the oval has margin (max_error 0.017 against a 0.06 limit). I therefore move the sensors to y 0.075, as the Integrator suggested, and keep the x positions, the 12 mm footprint and wheel_track 0.09. Against iteration 6 this is a single change, so any result can be attributed to look-ahead. Expected result: slalom losses at or below 1.0 with progress above 0.26, s-bend holding 19 or more finishes, and oval still 20 of 20. Risk: the extra look-ahead adds lag, which would show as higher oval max_error. If that happens, return to y 0.07.
